# Charger Logistics and Aurora to Begin Scaling Autonomous Fleet to 500 Trucks


October 26, 2026 9:00am EDT[Download as PDF](https://ir.aurora.tech/_assets/_b43b1c20802e72db7dcf51238ac7febe/aurora/news/2026-10-26_Charger_Logistics_and_Aurora_to_Begin_Scaling_154.pdf)


*Charger initiates plans to own and operate hundreds of driverless trucks on routes across the country, months after its initial Aurora contract*


DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Aurora Innovation, Inc. (NASDAQ: AUR), the leader in self-driving freight, today announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Charger Logistics under which Charger intends to purchase up to 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks. The agreement builds upon Charger’s existing contract signed in July, underscoring the carrier’s belief that the Aurora Driver will be critical to expanding its network and strengthening its business.


This press release features multimedia. View the full release here:[https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261026473142/en/](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261026473142/en/)


An Aurora Driver-powered truck hauling freight for Charger Logistics with no one behind the wheel in Texas. Charger plans to purchase up to 500 Aurora driverless trucks. Credit: Aurora


“Since launching autonomous operations along the Laredo corridor, we’ve realized immediate operational benefits that point to a clear path to scaling,” said Andy Khera, President of Charger Logistics. “Aurora’s plans to open long-haul, high-volume routes position us to scale geographically while we integrate autonomy from our TMS to the road, building a resilient and autonomous ecosystem for our customers."


“Andy and the team have decades of experience leveraging technology to move large volumes of freight across the continent, which makes owning driverless trucks a natural next step,” said Zac Andreoni, Vice President of Business Development at Aurora. “Owning the physical asset is the logical choice for our customers: it makes today’s operations more efficient and enables carriers to grow their business, keeping them competitive.”


**Path to Owning 500 Driverless Trucks**


Charger Logistics operates across the U.S. and Mexico, moving goods for the food and beverage, pharmaceutical, automotive, and retail industries. Under the non-binding MOU, the carrier would purchase 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks with delivery taking place over 2027 and 2028. Charger plans to deploy the trucks on current and new high-volume routes near the border and throughout the country.


Upon the final agreement, Charger intends to subscribe to Aurora’s Driver as a Service (DaaS) model, where ownership over the physical asset allows them to maximize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) savings. In parallel, Aurora benefits from an expected high-margin, capital-efficient, and asset-light business. DaaS agreements are a critical component to Aurora’s plan to scale to[30,000 driverless trucks in 2030](https://ir.aurora.tech/news-events/press-releases/detail/152/aurora-outlines-2030-vision-to-scale-to-30000-driverless-trucks-at-analyst-and-investor-day) . Additional Aurora customers are pursuing DaaS contracts to own and operate their own fleets of driverless trucks, demonstrating both the demand for autonomous trucks at scale and the confidence customers have in Aurora to deliver.


“With the launch of our second-generation hardware and trucks, Aurora is ready to support our customers' ambitions to grow their networks and move more freight with driverless trucks,” added Andreoni.


**About Aurora**


[Aurora](https://aurora.tech/) (Nasdaq: AUR) is delivering the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly to make transportation safer, increasingly accessible, and more reliable and efficient than ever before.[The Aurora Driver](https://aurora.tech/) is a self-driving system designed to operate multiple vehicle types, from freight-hauling trucks to ride-hailing passenger vehicles, and underpins Aurora's driver as a service product for trucking. Aurora is working with industry leaders across the transportation ecosystem, including AUMOVIO, FedEx, Hirschbach, McLane, NVIDIA, PACCAR, Ryder, Schneider, Toyota, Uber, Uber Freight, Volvo Trucks, Volvo Autonomous Solutions, and Werner. To learn more, visit[aurora.tech](https://aurora.tech/) .


**About Charger Logistics**


Charger Logistics USA is a privately held, asset-based transportation and logistics company operating across the United States and Mexico. Charger provides truckload, dedicated, temperature-controlled, and cross-border services, supported by a warehousing and cold storage network that enables end-to-end management of the full supply chain ecosystem. Charger operates on a proprietary transportation management system and a suite of in-house applications, delivering real-time visibility, execution, and data-driven decision-making across its network. Charger serves customers in food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, automotive, retail, and consumer products. To learn more, visit[chargerlogistics.com](http://chargerlogistics.com/) .
